TLDR: I unnecessarily lost enamel (the outer layer of my teeth), experienced jaw lock from an oversized mouth prop, and wasted money on assumed cavities. Good things = cute interior design.

This was a lesson I learned from Haus Clinic, and I hope it helps with your future dental visits.

Context:
- Went in for a routine dental hygiene check.
- Requested an X-ray from the dentist to check for cavities, just to be safe.
- The dentist insisted that I had 8 cavities.
- I was surprised since the dentist had just commented on the cleanliness of my teeth, noting barely any tartar, and I’ve never had more than 1-2 cavities in any of my annual check-ups, if any at all.
- I should have paused then, but I allowed the dentist to proceed with filling 4 of them.

Issue 1: Jaw Lock
- The dentist likely used an oversized mouth prop.
- I experienced jaw lock (for the first time in my life) during the 4 fillings.

Issue 2: Questionable Diagnosis
- Doubtful of the diagnosis, I went for X-rays and second opinions at two separate dental clinics.
- Both clinics noted that the areas identified as cavities by Haus were radiolucencies (darker areas on an X-ray where the teeth are less dense), but they weren't definitive enough to be considered cavities.
- The best practice would have been to monitor the areas for 3-6 months to see if there was any progression, instead of hastily removing enamel and risking a false positive.
- I waited and had the areas rechecked, and they remained unchanged, with some even increasing in density.
- So, it seems I lost part of my enamel unnecessarily.

Issue 3: Unnecessary Cost
- I wasted money on fillings that may not have been needed. But, as the saying goes, “never ask a barber if you need a haircut.”

Conclusion:
This could have been due to:
- Haus Clinic’s malpractice.
- The malpractice of a visiting dentist whom Haus didn’t properly screen.
- A naive dentist whom Haus did not screen thoroughly.

Place: very clean and well maintained
Tools and equipments: much better than other places that I’ve seen
Staffs and procedures: friendly and well organized

Summary: quality to cost ratio is very high ✨
